newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Haw Par sees leisure, healthcare growth.
newsitem.headline: Haw Par sees leisure, healthcare growth.

text.p: Haw Par Brothers International Ltd, maker of Tiger Balm, reported on Wednesday a 7.0 percent drop in 1996 profits, but some analysts still recommended a buy on the pharmaceutical and leisure company,
"Their core business operations are growing and prospects look good in the long run," said an analyst at a local bank.
"I would recommend a buy on Haw Par stocks at Singapore $3.00 (US$2.10) but would sell at S$3.40-3.50," he said.
Haw Par stocks ended at S$3.06 on 225,000 lots on Wednesday.
The company reported a 7.0 percent profit drop to S$32.91 million for year ended December 31, 1996. Turnover rose 5.0 percent to S$340.65 million.
According to The Estimate Directory, its 1996 net profit was expected to average around S$31.7 million.
It said in a statement accompanying its results that earnings fell due to a drop in investment income and inclusion of a once-off tax exempt dividend of S$9.23 million in 1995.
"The company's net profit grew by 26 percent if the S$9.23 million tax exempt dividend in 1995 is not considered," president and chief executive Hong Hai said at a news conference.

Hong said healthcare and leisure, which saw contributions grow 33 percent last year, will remain key revenue generators. "Organic growth continues in our two core areas. Outlook is positive because of their high growth prospects in Asia," he said.
Haw Par's expansion strategy includes forming alliances with existing partners like Malaysia's Lion Group and Brunswick of the United States.
On healthcare, Haw Par plans to step up its advertising and promotions to gain market share.
Haw Par will launch its Tiger Medical brand in India later this year, targeting India's 300-million-strong middle-class.
A 10 million ringgit healthcare plant to manufacture generic drugs is also scheduled to be opened in Malaysia this year.
On the leisure side, about S$16 million of internal funds would be spent over the next two years for upgrading its Underwater World facility in Singapore's tourist resort island of Sentosa.
It was looking to open more aquariums in Malaysia, China and other Asian countries, Hong said. (US$1=S$1.43)
